## 1. Current Situation or Progress since Last Week

### Systematic Literature Review

#### What I planned

- Try to add more filters or phrase combinations to reduce the number of paper to screen.
- start on screening Stream C (decision making on dynamic networks)

#### What I did

- Added some keywords to filter the papers further so that no re-search is needed (reported under PRISMA 2020 items 8 and 24c),
    - Streams A and C: six filter rules applied to the existing search results removed 325 records before screening
    - Stream B: one new search version (31 Oct) dropped papers that predict locations or activities, 63 records
- Finished screening stream A and B
    - stream A: 217 excluded, 154 goes into full text screening
    - stream B: 195 excluded, 58 goes into full text screening
- Checked my own screening consistency by screening 20 stream A records twice, at least a day apart
    - 17 of 20 agree (85%), Cohen's kappa 0.74, and the three differences were all stricter the second time
- Started citation chaining and handpicking using tools like ResearchRabbit (reported under PRISMA 2020 item 6)
    - stream B: added 41 records (54 found, 13 already in the screening pool)
    - the 41 records go straight to full text screening

#### What obstacles I found

- Have not fully grasped the theoretical background of Stream C, so the screening was postponed
    - Title and abstract screening did not finish by the planned date (Wed 4 Nov): 242 records remain, 241 of them in stream C

#### What I am currently doing

- reading AI-assisted teaching deck sourced from *Introduction to stochastic actor-based models for network dynamics* by Snijders et al. (2010)
- screening the 241 undecided stream C records, title first

#### What I am going to do next

- Finish the title and abstract screening for all records
- Full text screening on stream A
- Full text screening on stream B (58 records, plus the 41 citation chaining records)

### Inferring Social Ties from GPS Data

#### What I planned

- Start deep reading on stream B papers so that I can initiate work on inferring social ties from GPS data available

#### What I did

- collected stream B records' full-text document
- Sorted 160 papers into five groups by what each paper does: the stream B records marked include, unsure or background, plus method papers added from outside the stream
    - 38 core papers on inferring ties from mobility data
    - 26 papers that sharpen a method
    - 59 papers that train a method on pairs with known friendship
    - 14 papers that use known friends to predict places
    - 23 papers dropped
- Wrote structured reading notes with AI assistance: the formulas, the settings and the data each method needs
- Prepared the real GPS data on my own machine with IDs replaced by codes. The data stays there
- Ran a first set of methods on a simulated city where friends, coworkers and strangers are known
    - One finding: counting shared visits ranks coworkers above friends. This is one simulated city, so I treat it as exploratory

#### What obstacles I found

- Some papers could not be obtained through HU subscriptions
    - 7 of 160 papers have no file, and 5 more have a short or unreadable file
    - No file: Ma 2025, Socievole 2014, Steurer 2013, Li 2023, Nguyen 2022, Mounica 2020, He 2020

#### What I am currently doing

- checking the reading notes against the PDF pages, formula by formula
- reading the papers that train a method on pairs with known friendship

#### What I am going to do next

- Work out how to tell friendship from plain proximity (feedback from the 2 Nov group meeting)
- Run the methods on the real GPS data, after the checks on the simulated city pass

## 2. Points of Discussion

### What I want to confirm

- One reviewer, me, screens all records of the review. I checked my own consistency by screening 20 stream A records twice (17 of 20 agree, Cohen's kappa 0.74) and will report this in the limitations. I want to confirm that this design is acceptable.

### What obstacles I cannot decide on my own

- The terms for using the GPS data, and what I may report from it. Type of stuck:
    - not enough information, because the data owner's conditions on analysis and publication are not clear to me.

## 3. Definitions of Terms

::: {.table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Definitions of terms"}
| Term        | Definition                                                                 |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stream A    | Choice modeling affected by social interactions or peer-effects            |
| Stream B    | Social ties or social networks inference from GPS Data                     |
| Stream C    | Dynamic networks                                                           |
| Social ties | Links or relationship between one person to another in a specific settings |
| GPS Data    | Movement tracking data obtained by providers                               |
| Title and abstract screening | First pass over the records: I read only the title and abstract and mark each record include, unsure or exclude. |
| Full text screening | Second pass: I read the whole paper and decide whether it meets the inclusion criteria of the review. |
| Citation chaining | Finding further papers by following the reference lists of known papers (backward) and the papers that cite them (forward). |
| Filter rules | Fixed rules that remove records before anyone reads them, for example by document type, language or missing key words. Every removed record stays in the sheet with its reason. |
| PRISMA 2020 | A reporting guideline for systematic reviews. It lists what a review should report, such as the sources searched, the screening method and a flow diagram of record counts. |
| Cohen's kappa | A measure of agreement between two screening passes that removes the agreement expected by chance. 1 is perfect agreement and 0 is chance level. |
| Shared visit (co-location) | Two people recorded at the same place in the same time window. |
| Proximity versus friendship | Proximity means two people are near each other. Friendship needs more, because coworkers share a place every day without being friends. |
| Stochastic actor-based model | A model of how a network changes over time: each person adds, keeps or drops ties in small steps, and the model estimates the rules behind those choices. |
:::
